reason.description: Optional: closing reason/comment. Required for "decision items" of the checklist (for example, refusing a book promotion): such an item is closed by a SEPARATE call with an explicit reason, not silently in a common batch.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

ids.description: List of task IDs to close

description: Fill in the antagonist (BB): name/description/motive/resources/timeline (≥3 steps)/reaction to defeat.
name: setAntagonist

textId.description: Slug identifier of the antagonist, format [a-z0-9-]+. Unique; used by hints/encounters/items for references (`relatedTextIds`/`npcTextId` etc.) the same way as textId of keyNpcs/nodes.

name.description: Name/title of the antagonist. Unique, may be conventional if the BB is an organization/phenomenon ("The Cult of the Nameless", "Winter").

description.description: BB description: who it is, what it looks like, how the party learns about it. Several sentences, no stats/CR.

motive.description: Motive: what it wants and WHY. Must be understandable and (ideally) not banally villainous. "Revenge for an executed brother", "does not want its native element to vanish", not "wants to rule the world".

resources.description: Antagonist resources: what it has at its disposal (minions, artifacts, factions, information). Brief, without stat blocks.

timeline.description: BB plan timeline: what will happen without the party's intervention. Each step — what and under which conditions/time. At least 3 steps for a five-beat arc.

trigger.description: Step trigger: time or condition. "After 3 days of inaction", "after the key witness dies", "when the party uncovers the first ritual".

event.description: What happens at this step. A concrete event that changes the game world. "A victim in the main square", "a second cultist arrives with reinforcements".

onDefeat.description: Reaction to the party's defeat/retreat: what the BB will do if the party fails on the first attempt or retreats altogether. Not "returns and kills everyone", but concretely: "goes underground, a season later raises a cult in the neighboring city".

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Fill in the book metadata: title, setting, tone/genre, target level, duration.
name: setMetadata

title.description: Adventure title. Localized to the generation language (up to 200 characters recommended).

setting.description: Setting/world in one or two sentences: where it takes place, what is special. For example: "A coastal town on the border with an elven forest, after a recent magical catastrophe".

toneAndGenre.description: Tone/genre: "gloomy detective story", "heroic fantasy", "comic caper", "political intrigue", "horror", "epic".

targetLevel.description: Target character level and difficulty: "1-3, beginners", "5-7, medium", "10+, hardcore". LEVEL only, NOT the number of heroes: the book is playable both solo and in a group — the headcount is not baked in.

expectedDuration.description: Expected duration: "3-4 hours per session", "a short campaign of 5-7 sessions", "one-shot".

tags.description: 5-10 tags for search/filtering in the UI: genre ("horror"/"detective"), setting ("Forgotten Realms"/"Slavic fantasy"), themes ("dragons"/"undead"/"politics"), features ("for beginners"/"lots of battles"/"roleplay-heavy"). The same requirements as in book_description: genre+setting+themes+features.

author.description: Author: if the structure was extracted from an uploaded book — the real author/publisher from the copyright page. If the structure was generated from scratch — null (there is no living author, the generator is not an author).

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo
